hero.headline: US forces shoot down Iranian drones in Strait of Hormuz as peace talks continue
hero.body:
US Central Command announced that American forces destroyed multiple Iranian one-way attack drones targeting commercial vessels in the Strait of Hormuz. The military action occurred as diplomatic negotiations between Washington and Tehran remain ongoing, though prospects for a quick resolution appear uncertain.

Centcom stated that Iran launched the drones at commercial ships transiting the strategic waterway. US forces intercepted and destroyed the weapons before they could reach their targets. The command did not specify the exact number of drones involved or identify which commercial ships were threatened.

The drone attack happened following a week of heightened tensions between the two countries. Despite military confrontations, US and Iranian negotiators have continued working toward a peace agreement to end hostilities in the region. President Trump initially suggested that a preliminary deal could be finalized over the weekend, but later distanced himself from those comments with social media posts describing Iranian officials as "very dishonorable people to deal with."

The Strait of Hormuz serves as a critical chokepoint for global energy supplies, with approximately one-fifth of the world's petroleum passing through the narrow passage. Any sustained conflict in the area threatens international shipping and global oil markets.

The timing of the attack underscores the fragility of the diplomatic process. Both countries have maintained diplomatic channels while military incidents continue to occur, creating uncertainty about whether negotiations can succeed. Conflicting claims from US and Iranian officials about the state of negotiations have added to confusion about the prospects for peace.

Trump's statements have sent mixed signals about the negotiations. After suggesting earlier in the week that progress was being made, he reversed course and criticized the Iranian government's negotiating position and intentions. Iranian media outlets have reported that an agreement was near completion, but the US president dismissed these claims.

The incident also comes as Iran prepares for an unprecedented World Cup appearance on American soil. The Iranian national team will compete in the United States despite ongoing hostilities, marking the first time a country at war with the host nation has participated in the tournament. The team's opening match against New Zealand in Los Angeles is scheduled to take place amid continuing tensions.

Neither the Pentagon nor the State Department has issued comprehensive statements explaining how the drone attack might affect ongoing peace negotiations. The incident demonstrates the complicated security situation in the Persian Gulf, where military confrontations can happen simultaneously with diplomatic efforts. The challenge facing both nations is whether they can maintain negotiations despite armed conflicts continuing to unfold.

cards.headline: Israel Launches Airstrikes on Lebanon Amid Iran Peace Talks
cards.teaser: Israeli forces carried out air strikes on Lebanon as diplomatic efforts intensify to end the U.S.-Iran conflict.
cards.body:
Israel conducted airstrikes on Lebanon, according to state media reports. The strikes occurred as diplomatic efforts between the U.S. and Iran intensified, with Trump announcing he was canceling planned missile strikes against Iran after two days of escalating attacks.

Trump claimed Washington and Tehran were on the verge of signing a peace agreement. However, Iran's foreign ministry dismissed this, stating that no final decision on an agreement had been reached. Pakistan's prime minister, acting as a key mediator, said a deal was likely expected within 24 hours, though officials on both sides acknowledged the agreement could still fall through.

cards.headline: Trump announces killing of Venezuelan gang leader in US military strike
cards.teaser: President Trump said US Southern Command conducted a strike that killed the leader of Tren de Aragua.
cards.body:
President Trump announced that the US military killed Hector Rusthenford Guerrero Flores, leader of the Venezuelan gang Tren de Aragua, in a "swift and lethal kinetic strike." Trump made the announcement on his Truth Social platform, describing the operation as carried out by US Southern Command with assistance from Venezuela.

Guerrero Flores, also known as Niño Guerrero, led one of the region's most violent criminal organizations that originated in Venezuela. Trump characterized Tren de Aragua as a terrorist organization responsible for bloodshed across the Western Hemisphere.

cards.headline: Warrantless surveillance program lapses as Congress fails to extend FISA authority
cards.teaser: Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act expired after both chambers failed to pass extension bills.
cards.body:
The Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act's Section 702 authority expired after both the House and Senate failed to pass legislation extending the warrantless surveillance program. The lapse occurred amid opposition from Democrats and marks the first time the surveillance powers have been allowed to expire.

The expiration creates legal uncertainty about the extent to which the US can conduct surveillance of foreigners located abroad. Section 702 had been set to expire, but lawmakers attempted to pass bills extending the authority through July 2. The program allows intelligence agencies to monitor foreign targets without obtaining individual warrants.

cards.headline: Ukraine Running Low on Patriot Missiles as Russia Maintains Stockpile
cards.teaser: Ukraine is depleting its supply of American-made Patriot interceptors and has requested additional air defense systems.
cards.body:
Ukraine is running out of American-made Patriot air defense interceptors as Russia continues to possess substantial ballistic missile capabilities. Ukrainian officials are appealing to the United States and allies for more interceptor missiles to defend against ongoing attacks.

The shortage of Patriots leaves Ukraine with fewer options to stop Russian ballistic missile strikes. Russia maintains a large inventory of ballistic missiles, giving it a sustained offensive capability. The imbalance in air defense resources has become a critical concern for Ukrainian military planners as the conflict continues.

cards.headline: Commerce Department orders Anthropic to shut down AI models over security concerns
cards.body:
The Commerce Department has directed Anthropic to shut down its Fable and Mythos AI models, citing national security concerns over a potential vulnerability in the Fable 5 system. The government action targets what officials describe as a jailbreak that could pose security risks.

Anthropic has publicly disputed the government's decision to recall the models. In a blog post, the company stated it disagrees that discovering a narrow potential jailbreak justifies pulling a commercial model deployed to hundreds of millions of people. The company's response signals tension between AI safety protocols and government oversight.

The shutdown comes amid a broader conflict between Anthropic and the Trump administration. The Pentagon previously designated Anthropic as a "supply chain risk," the first time this blacklisting tool has been used against a U.S. company. In response, Anthropic filed two lawsuits against the Department of Defense, alleging that the government's decision was unlawful and violated the company's First Amendment rights.

According to Anthropic, the conflict stems from the company's attempt to implement safeguards against the military's potential use of its AI models for mass domestic surveillance or fully autonomous lethal weapons. The company accused the Trump administration and Pentagon of pursuing "punitive actions" against it for refusing to comply with ideological demands from the government. In its California lawsuit, Anthropic stated that "the constitution does not allow the government to wield its enormous power to punish a company for its protected speech."

Despite the legal dispute, Anthropic emphasized its commitment to national security. The company noted that its AI model Claude has been deeply integrated into the Department of Defense over the past year and was previously the only AI model approved for use in classified systems. Anthropic stated it had collaborated with the Pentagon to modify its systems for specific military needs and wanted to continue such negotiations.

A company spokesperson said that seeking judicial review did not change Anthropic's "longstanding commitment to harnessing AI to protect our national security," but that legal action was necessary "to protect our business, our customers and our partners." The company indicated it would pursue dialogue with the government alongside its court challenges.

In its lawsuit, Anthropic alleged that the government's actions were "harming Anthropic irreparably" by seeking to "destroy the economic value created by one of the world's fastest-growing private companies." However, Anthropic's CEO had previously told CBS News that the supply chain risk designation's impact was "fairly small" and the company would be "gonna be fine."

The shutdown represents a significant intervention in the commercial AI sector, affecting models that had reached widespread deployment. The incident raises questions about the balance between innovation and security concerns, as well as the extent of federal authority over AI development and deployment.

cards.headline: SpaceX completes initial public offering
cards.teaser: The space company transitioned to public ownership, with investors now holding stakes in the business.
cards.body:
SpaceX has gone public in what founder Elon Musk described as "the largest IPO ever." The company, which Musk said had less than a 10% chance of success when it started, has now transitioned from private to publicly traded ownership.

With the IPO complete, SpaceX is now owned by investors expecting financial returns. The company's valuation reflects its potential in artificial intelligence alongside its space operations business.

hero.headline: Swiss Voters to Decide on Population Cap at 10 Million
hero.teaser: Switzerland will hold a referendum on limiting its population to 10 million people in a measure that would curb migration.
hero.body:
Switzerland is holding a referendum on a proposal to cap the country's population at 10 million. The far-right initiative would require the government to implement restrictions on family reunification, residency permits, and asylum if the population reaches 9.5 million before 2050. The Swiss People's Party frames the plan as a sustainability measure.

Opponents warn the proposal would be economically devastating. Critics argue it would create chaos and harm Switzerland's economy by restricting migration. The ballot concludes this weekend, with Swiss voters making the final decision on whether to adopt the population limit.

cards.headline: Israel Launches Airstrikes on Lebanon Amid Iran Peace Talks
cards.teaser: Israeli forces carried out air strikes on Lebanon as diplomatic efforts intensify to end the U.S.-Iran conflict.
cards.body:
Israel conducted airstrikes on Lebanon, according to state media reports. The strikes occurred as diplomatic efforts between the U.S. and Iran intensified, with Trump announcing he was canceling planned missile strikes against Iran after two days of escalating attacks.

Trump claimed Washington and Tehran were on the verge of signing a peace agreement. However, Iran's foreign ministry dismissed this, stating that no final decision on an agreement had been reached. Pakistan's prime minister, acting as a key mediator, said a deal was likely expected within 24 hours, though officials on both sides acknowledged the agreement could still fall through.

cards.headline: Ebola Outbreak in Congo Kills at Least 140 People
cards.teaser: Aid agencies are mobilizing to help health workers in the Democratic Republic of Congo combat a deadly Ebola outbreak.
cards.body:
An Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has killed at least 140 people. Aid agencies are mobilizing to support health workers responding to the crisis, though officials warn the actual death toll may be considerably higher than confirmed figures.

The virus has spread through communities in the Congo, triggering an urgent international health response. Ebola's high mortality rate makes rapid containment efforts essential to prevent further transmission.

cards.headline: Ukraine Running Low on Patriot Missiles as Russia Maintains Stockpile
cards.teaser: Ukraine is depleting its supply of American-made Patriot interceptors and has requested additional air defense systems.
cards.body:
Ukraine is running out of American-made Patriot air defense interceptors as Russia continues to possess substantial ballistic missile capabilities. Ukrainian officials are appealing to the United States and allies for more interceptor missiles to defend against ongoing attacks.

The shortage of Patriots leaves Ukraine with fewer options to stop Russian ballistic missile strikes. Russia maintains a large inventory of ballistic missiles, giving it a sustained offensive capability. The imbalance in air defense resources has become a critical concern for Ukrainian military planners as the conflict continues.

cards.headline: UK Defense Secretary Resigns Over Military Funding Dispute
cards.teaser: John Healey stepped down after seeking to join a global investment bank to raise defense funds, warning of resource shortages.
cards.body:
John Healey resigned as UK Defense Secretary after attempting to have Britain join a global investment bank to raise military funding. His departure represents a fresh setback for Prime Minister Keir Starmer and comes amid warnings about insufficient resources for rising security threats.

Healey's exit follows disputes over defense spending levels and the military's capacity to address mounting challenges. The resignation of a top defense official raises questions about Britain's military readiness and the government's ability to secure adequate funding for national security priorities.

cards.headline: Iranian Regime More Willing to Take Risks After Leadership Change
cards.teaser: The war has produced new Iranian leaders who believe they have absorbed the worst pressure from America and Israel.
cards.body:
Iran's new leaders, brought to power following conflict with the United States, are more willing to take risks than their predecessors. These leaders believe Iran has already endured the most severe actions that America and Israel can deliver, according to analysts monitoring negotiations.

This shift in Iran's leadership approach has altered diplomatic dynamics as peace talks progress. The regime's increased tolerance for confrontation marks a significant change in how Iran conducts negotiations and manages regional conflicts.

cards.headline: Brazilians Paint Streets to Support National Team at World Cup
cards.teaser: After years of muted enthusiasm, Brazilians are reviving the tradition of painting streets in support of their football team.
cards.body:
After years of waning interest in the World Cup, Brazilians are rekindling their passion for the tournament. The revival of enthusiasm is visible across the country, where citizens are painting streets as a colorful show of support for their national team.

This street painting tradition represents a cultural ritual that had faded during previous World Cup cycles. As excitement builds around the team's prospects, Brazilians are embracing the practice once again, transforming public spaces into vibrant displays of national pride.

hero.headline: Workers remove Trump's name from Kennedy Center following court order
hero.body:
Workers began removing Donald Trump's name from the Kennedy Center's facade early Saturday morning, hours after a federal court deadline passed on Friday night. The removal work started in the pre-dawn hours after an emergency appeal to block the removal was rejected by an appeals court.

The Kennedy Center had missed a two-week court-ordered deadline to remove the words "The Donald J Trump and" from its exterior by Friday at 11:59pm. U.S. District Judge Christopher Cooper had previously ruled that Trump's name had been illegally added to the building and ordered its removal.

Trump's name was added to the Kennedy Center last December after his hand-picked board of trustees voted unanimously to rename the venue. The board consisted of trustees Trump selected after removing the 18 members appointed by former President Joe Biden. Trump also made himself chair of the board and seized control of the venue in February.

The Kennedy Center was originally designated by Congress as a living memorial to President John F. Kennedy and opened in 1971. Judge Cooper wrote in his 94-page opinion that "Congress gave the Kennedy Center its name, and only Congress can change it." The legal challenge was brought by Joyce Beatty, a Democratic representative from Ohio and ex-officio member of the Kennedy Center's board.

Workers erected scaffolding Friday evening and draped tarpaulin over the temporary structure at 2am to block public views. Despite the covering, workers were observed removing the letters around 3am. A crowd of more than 100 people gathered at a "Hands Off the Arts" rally in front of the center to witness the removal, with attendees chanting "Shame!" and "Take it down."

Trump and his legal team mounted a last-minute effort to keep his name on the building less than 36 hours before the deadline. At 1pm Friday, Judge Cooper ruled that Trump's lawyers had failed to demonstrate they were likely to win an appeal or that the Kennedy Center would suffer "irreparable harm" if the name was removed.

Justice Department lawyers then appealed Cooper's decision at 3:46pm, arguing to the appeals court that it made no sense to alter the signage only to potentially revert the name again after a successful appeal. This second emergency appeal was denied shortly after 7pm.

The Kennedy Center had already removed Trump's name from its website and sent emails offering tickets to events at "the Kennedy Center" without reference to Trump. The venue continued operating its regular programming schedule during the removal process.

Judge Cooper also issued a temporary block on Trump's demand to close the Kennedy Center for two years of renovations, which was scheduled to begin in July. Trump subsequently announced he was giving up control of the venue.

cards.headline: Police officer removed from duty after allegations of using AI to fabricate evidence
cards.teaser: A criminal investigation has been launched after an officer was accused of using artificial intelligence to create evidence.
cards.body:
A police officer in Derbyshire has been removed from frontline duties and is under criminal investigation for allegedly using artificial intelligence to create evidence. The officer is suspected of fabricating evidential material across multiple cases.

The investigation marks the first known case of its kind in the UK. The officer faces allegations of perverting the course of justice through the use of the technology. Police have not disclosed the officer's identity or provided further details about the affected cases.

cards.headline: Israel conducts air strikes on Lebanon as Iran reports progress on US negotiations
cards.teaser: Israeli forces carried out air strikes on targets in Lebanon, according to state media, while Iran's foreign minister said a deal with the United States is near.
cards.body:
Israel launched air strikes on Lebanon, according to state media reports in the region. The strikes occurred as diplomatic negotiations continued between Iran and the United States.

Iran's foreign minister claimed that negotiations with the United States to end fighting were nearing completion. However, U.S. President Trump dismissed these claims, distancing himself from earlier comments suggesting a deal could be signed soon. Trump posted angry messages on social media describing Iranians as "very dishonorable people to deal with," casting doubt on the Iranian government's assertions about progress toward an agreement.

cards.headline: Haiti returns to World Cup after 52 years as nation seeks peace amid conflict
cards.teaser: Haiti's men's soccer team is competing in the World Cup for the first time in more than five decades as the country faces internal strife.
cards.body:
Haiti's national soccer team made its first appearance at a men's World Cup in 52 years. The team's participation comes as the Caribbean nation continues to face significant internal conflict and gang violence that has affected daily life across the country.

The World Cup appearance represents a moment of hope and unity for Haiti. Gang leaders themselves are reportedly soccer lovers, and the tournament provides citizens with a shared source of pride during a period of instability and insecurity.

cards.headline: Therapeutic food shortages hit Senegal program for malnourished children
cards.teaser: A program that provided easy access to lifesaving therapeutic food for malnourished children in Senegal is now facing shortages.
cards.body:
An innovative program in Senegal had successfully provided therapeutic food to treat malnourished children, giving parents easy access to the specialized nutrition product. The program was working effectively until recent shortages emerged.

Health specialists attribute the supply disruptions to cuts in U.S. foreign aid funding. The reduction in aid has disrupted the supply chain that kept the therapeutic food available to families who need it most.

cards.headline: Working-class Indian women direct documentary about their own lives
cards.teaser: Ten women from a working-class Indian community were given smartphones to film a documentary about their daily experiences.
cards.body:
A group of ten working-class women from an Indian community were given smartphones and trained to direct a documentary called Cool Ladies Club. The project centered on capturing the lives and experiences of women whose stories are typically absent from mainstream media.

By putting the filmmaking tools directly in the hands of the participants, the documentary reflects their own perspectives and priorities rather than an outside filmmaker's interpretation. The resulting film showcases aspects of working-class life that rarely appear on screen, told by the women living those experiences.

cards.headline: Rugby star Kevin Sinfield knighted as authors Blackman and Donaldson made dames
cards.teaser: A new honors list includes a knighthood for rugby league player Kevin Sinfield and damehoods for children's authors Malorie Blackman and Julia Donaldson.
cards.body:
Rugby league star Kevin Sinfield has been knighted in the latest honours list. The recognition acknowledges his contributions to sport and charitable endeavours.

Children's authors Malorie Blackman and Julia Donaldson have been made dames in the same honours list. Blackman is known for writing the Noughts and Crosses series, while Donaldson created The Gruffalo. Both authors have had a significant impact on children's literature.

hero.headline: Justice Department Approves Paramount-Warner Bros. Merger
hero.body:
The Justice Department has cleared the way for Paramount Skydance to acquire Warner Bros. Discovery in an $111 billion deal that will reshape the media landscape. The approval came after an eight-month antitrust investigation, concluding that the merger poses no threat to competition or consumers.

The combined company will control major film studios, streaming platforms, cable networks, and news operations. Paramount brings CBS, CBS News, Paramount Pictures, and the Paramount+ streaming service to the transaction. Warner Bros. Discovery contributes HBO, Max, the Discovery Channel, and Warner Bros. Studios. The merger will place CNN and CBS News under the same corporate ownership.

The Justice Department's antitrust division completed its analysis after reviewing over two million documents from more than 80 custodians and receiving extensive input from third parties across the media and entertainment sector. In a statement, the agency said it found the transaction unlikely to harm competition in streaming video on demand, linear television, or studio development and distribution of theatrical films.

Paramount responded positively to the approval, calling the deal "pro-competitive" and saying it will create "a stronger company better positioned to compete against dominant technology platforms." The company characterized the merger as beneficial for consumers, creators, and the entertainment industry.

However, obstacles remain. The UK's Competition and Markets Authority has opened an investigation into the merger, setting a deadline of August 7 to decide whether a more detailed review is needed. European regulators are also examining the funding behind the deal, which includes $24 billion in commitments from Gulf sovereign-wealth funds. Australia has already approved the merger, determining it is unlikely to substantially lessen competition in theatrical film distribution.

Staff at CNN and CBS News have raised concerns about the combination, worried about potential job cuts and editorial changes. Paramount has promised $6 billion in cost savings from the merger. There is also speculation about potential changes to CNN's editorial direction under Paramount Skydance leadership, though David Ellison pledged in March that the network's editorial independence would be protected.

State-level opposition could pose additional challenges. California Attorney General Rob Bonta stated that the merger "remains under investigation" by his office and is "not a done deal." Multiple state attorneys general could potentially file a lawsuit to block the transaction in coming weeks.

Critics of the deal have expressed concerns about media consolidation. Craig Aaron, co-chief executive of Free Press, called the approval troubling, saying it concentrates too much media power in one corporation. Democratic Senator Elizabeth Warren also criticized the decision, arguing the merger allows aligned billionaires to control media consumption and pricing.

The deal now moves toward final closing procedures, including shareholder votes and remaining regulatory requirements across jurisdictions where both companies operate.

cards.headline: SpaceX Closes First Trading Day Up 19% in Record Market Debut
cards.teaser: Elon Musk's space company began trading on the Nasdaq and ended its first session valued at $2.2 trillion.
cards.body:
SpaceX made its market debut on the Nasdaq stock exchange, opening at $135 per share and closing at $161, a 19% gain on its first day of trading. The IPO valued the company at $2.2 trillion, making it the world's largest initial public offering.

The milestone also marked a historic moment for Elon Musk, whose net worth reached $1.11 trillion according to the Bloomberg rich list, making him the world's first trillionaire. The successful listing reflects SpaceX's evolution into a major player in commercial spaceflight and satellite communications.

cards.headline: Elon Musk Becomes First Person to Reach $1 Trillion Net Worth
cards.teaser: The SpaceX and Tesla CEO's wealth surpassed the trillion-dollar mark as SpaceX shares soared in their market debut.
cards.body:
Elon Musk has become the world's first trillionaire, with a net worth of $1.11 trillion according to the Bloomberg rich list. The milestone was reached as SpaceX launched its initial public offering on the Nasdaq stock exchange, valuing the space company at $2.2 trillion.

Musk's achievement parallels that of John D. Rockefeller, the oil magnate who became America's first billionaire in 1916. As head of X, Tesla, and SpaceX, Musk's ascent to trillionaire status represents an unprecedented concentration of personal wealth in modern times.

cards.headline: Oil Shipments Through Strait of Hormuz Remain Low Despite U.S. Naval Support
cards.teaser: Just over 200 commercial vessels have passed through the strategic waterway since U.S. intervention, far below pre-war levels.
cards.body:
Commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz has not returned to normal levels, even with U.S. military presence in the region. President Trump reported that more than 200 commercial vessels have successfully transited the strait, a significant decrease from historical traffic patterns.

The waterway remains crucial for global energy markets. The reduced tanker traffic continues to limit oil supplies worldwide, even as efforts to ease tensions with Iran advance.

cards.headline: Stock Markets Close Higher on Iran Deal Hopes and SpaceX Debut
cards.teaser: The Dow, S&P 500, and Nasdaq all posted gains as investors reacted to diplomatic developments and the SpaceX IPO.
cards.body:
U.S. stock indexes rose as President Trump canceled further Iran strikes and signaled progress toward a peace deal. However, Iran stated that an agreement has not yet been finalized. Oil prices fell on the diplomatic developments, while broader equity markets gained on reduced geopolitical tensions.

SpaceX made its market debut on the Nasdaq with a valuation of $2.2 trillion. The listing bolstered investor sentiment, with Elon Musk becoming the world's first trillionaire, according to the Bloomberg rich list, with a net worth of $1.11 trillion.

cards.headline: Tech Stock Surge Raises Concerns of Market Bubble
cards.teaser: Enthusiasm for technology shares has pushed valuations to levels that may not be sustainable, analysts warn.
cards.body:
SpaceX made its market debut on the Nasdaq with a valuation of $2.2 trillion, with shares surging 19% on the first day of trading. The listing propelled Elon Musk to a net worth of $1.11 trillion, making him the world's first trillionaire according to the Bloomberg rich list.

The IPO frenzy reflects broader enthusiasm in the technology sector, where investor demand has driven valuations to levels that concern some analysts. While genuine innovation supports some gains, the pace and magnitude of recent price increases prompt warnings that investors may be taking on excessive risk.

With the IPO complete, SpaceX is now owned by investors expecting financial returns. The company's valuation reflects its potential in artificial intelligence alongside its space operations business.

cards.headline: FBI opens replica town in Alabama for cyberattack training
cards.teaser: The bureau built a simulated small town inside a building to serve as a dedicated cyber training facility.
cards.body:
The FBI has constructed a replica small town inside a building in Alabama to serve as a dedicated training ground for cyberattack simulations. The facility allows agents to practice responses to cyber threats in a controlled environment that mirrors real-world conditions.

This physical infrastructure approach prepares personnel for potential digital attacks by enabling hands-on training exercises within the simulated town setting.

cards.headline: Researchers measure global fungal network length
cards.teaser: Scientists have quantified arbuscular mycorrhizal fungal networks, finding threads long enough to extend beyond the Solar System.
cards.body:
Researchers have completed measurements of arbuscular mycorrhizal fungal networks on a global scale, documenting both their length and mass. The study found that the combined threads would be long enough to reach beyond the Solar System.

Arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi form symbiotic relationships with plant roots and create extensive underground networks. The research provides the first comprehensive quantification of these networks across the planet.

cards.headline: Meta AI unit faces internal turmoil, report says
cards.teaser: Engineers inside Meta's AI unit, which employs 6,500 people, have described difficult working conditions.
cards.body:
Meta's newly established artificial intelligence division, which employs 6,500 people, is experiencing widespread employee dissatisfaction. Engineers working within the unit have described conditions as oppressive, with the workplace described as "soul-crushing."

The internal strife suggests the division is approaching a point of potential employee revolt. This turmoil comes as Meta continues pursuing its strategic expansion into artificial intelligence development.

cards.headline: NASA announces Artemis III crew assignments
cards.teaser: The space agency named crew members for the Artemis III mission planned for 2027.
cards.body:
NASA has announced the crew for Artemis III, scheduled for 2027. The four-person crew includes NASA astronauts Randy Bresnik, Frank Rubio, and Andre Douglas, along with European Space Agency astronaut Luca Parmitano. They will orbit Earth while practicing docking their Orion capsule with two lunar landers.

The announcement was made in Houston, following Artemis II's recent journey around the Moon. Unlike future Artemis missions, this crew will not land on the lunar surface or travel near it.

cards.headline: Andrew Yang identifies startup opportunities in lowering living costs
cards.teaser: The entrepreneur has compiled a list of areas where Americans overpay, suggesting these represent business opportunities.
cards.body:
Andrew Yang has identified reducing the cost of living as the next major startup opportunity. He compiled a list of sectors where Americans overpay, including housing, food, and wireless services.

Yang believes the next wave of successful startups will capitalize on this gap by returning money to consumers through lower-cost alternatives in these inflated markets. This represents a shift in focus from traditional tech startup models toward companies designed to address everyday expenses.

hero.headline: UFC to award record bonuses at White House event
hero.teaser: The promotion will hand out $400,000 for fight of the night and $425,000 for top performances Sunday.
hero.body:
The UFC will distribute its highest bonus payouts ever at Sunday's UFC Freedom 250 event being held at the White House. The fight of the night award will be worth $400,000, while the top individual performance bonuses will each total $425,000.

The record-breaking bonuses accompany what promises to be an unprecedented sporting event. The White House South Lawn has been transformed into a massive arena featuring a 92-foot steel structure nicknamed "the Claw," thousands of seats arranged in a mini coliseum configuration, and an octagon fighting cage.

The event coincides with President Donald Trump's 80th birthday and the nation's 250th anniversary celebration. About 4,300 military personnel are expected to attend the seven-fight card, which will unfold on the iconic lawn typically reserved for presidential travel and official state functions.

The setup has drawn legal scrutiny. Public Integrity Project filed a lawsuit in federal court seeking an emergency injunction to halt the event, arguing the administration violated multiple federal laws to accommodate what the group describes as a private, for-profit sporting enterprise masquerading as a patriotic celebration. The lawsuit names the National Park Service and Department of the Interior as defendants.

The legal challenge centers on whether the UFC event qualifies for exemptions under a temporary National Park Service rule designed for 250th anniversary events. The rule applies only to events "planned, organized and executed" by the federal government. The lawsuit contends that UFC Freedom 250, which CEO Dana White has indicated was Trump's idea, fails this test and instead constitutes a celebration of the UFC brand.

The suit also raised concerns about the Claw structure, alleging it was erected without required congressional authorization or mandatory environmental review. The massive steel structure has rerouted presidential travel and is visible from the front of the White House.

Trump's stock holdings in TKO Group Holdings, the UFC's parent company, also featured in conflict of interest allegations. Financial disclosures show Trump purchased between $25,000 and $50,000 worth of TKO stock in March.

A federal judge refused to block the event on Friday, allowing organizers to proceed with Sunday's spectacle.

The White House called the lawsuit "obstructionist, baseless, and dilatory," stating the event "will undoubtedly go down as one of the most historic sporting events in our Nation's history."

Weather could complicate Sunday's proceedings. The National Weather Service forecast for June 14 indicates a chance of showers and thunderstorms, with conditions expected to deteriorate into the evening when the main event is scheduled to begin.

cards.headline: Misiorowski strikes out 15 in one-hit shutout as Brewers blank Phillies
cards.teaser: Jacob Misiorowski struck out a career-high 15 batters and allowed just one hit in a complete game.
cards.body:
Jacob Misiorowski delivered a dominant performance Friday night, striking out a career-high 15 batters as the Milwaukee Brewers shut out the Philadelphia Phillies 6-0. The right-hander pitched a complete game, allowing just one hit in the victory.

Misiorowski's exceptional outing required no relief help, with the pitcher taking the shutout from start to finish. The Brewers' offense provided ample support with six runs, giving their starter all the cushion needed in the lopsided win.

cards.headline: Alvarez hits grand slam and two-run homer in same inning for Astros
cards.teaser: Yordan Alvarez launched two home runs in the first inning against Kansas City, driving in six runs.
cards.body:
Houston Astros' Yordan Alvarez delivered a dominant performance in the first inning against the Kansas City Royals on Friday night, hitting both a grand slam and a two-run homer. The back-to-back home runs gave the Astros an early offensive surge.

Alvarez's two-homer display in a single inning highlighted Houston's strong start in the game's opening frame.

cards.headline: Pulisic exits United States World Cup opener at halftime
cards.teaser: Christian Pulisic was substituted at halftime of the Americans' 3-0 lead over Paraguay.
cards.body:
Original Card Text

United States winger Christian Pulisic was removed from the World Cup opener against Paraguay at halftime on Friday, with his team holding a three-goal advantage. The Americans led 3-0 at the break when the substitution was made.

No immediate details were provided about the reason for the halftime change. The United States went on to win the match 4-1 despite Pulisic playing only the first half.

---

Note: The additional source material provided does not contain relevant information about the Pulisic substitution. The sources reference Scotland's World Cup opener and a police raid in Peru—different stories entirely. Therefore, I am returning the original card text unchanged, as instructed.

cards.headline: Balogun scores twice as United States defeats Paraguay 4-1 in World Cup opener
cards.teaser: The United States men's national team opened its 2026 World Cup campaign with a 4-1 victory over Paraguay on Friday, with striker Folarin Balogun netting two go.
cards.body:
Folarin Balogun netted two goals as the United States defeated Paraguay 4-1 in its World Cup opener on Friday. The Americans dominated the first half, building a 3-0 lead before the break. Balogun, who represented England and Nigeria at youth levels before choosing the USMNT, described the performance as a "dreamy night."

Christian Pulisic contributed to the strong opening-half showing before being substituted at halftime with the match already decided. The victory gives the United States three points and a commanding goal differential as it begins group stage play in the tournament held partially on American soil.

cards.headline: Dempsey criticizes Marsch over anthem comments
cards.teaser: The former national team star took issue with Marsch suggesting some players needed encouragement to sing.
cards.body:
Clint Dempsey, the US men's national team's joint all-time leading scorer, criticized Jesse Marsch after the Canada coach suggested American players needed to be encouraged to sing the national anthem. Marsch made the comments while praising Canada's pride ahead of their World Cup opener against Bosnia and Herzegovina on Friday.

Dempsey responded sharply, telling Marsch to focus on his own team. The exchange reflected disagreement over player conduct during the anthem, with Dempsey emphasizing that representing the country was an honor. Marsch served as a USMNT assistant from 2010 to 2011 before becoming Canada's coach two years ago.

cards.headline: Yankees manager says team owes Chapman no apology
cards.teaser: Aaron Boone responded to the Boston closer's claim he deserves an apology for his 2022 departure.
cards.body:
Aroldis Chapman expressed his belief that the Yankees owe him an apology for how the team handled his departure following the 2022 season. The closer, now with the Boston Red Sox, reiterated this position on Thursday.

Manager Aaron Boone responded Friday, rejecting Chapman's claim. Boone stated that the Yankees have no obligation to apologize to the pitcher for the circumstances surrounding his exit from New York.

hero.headline: Authors Malorie Blackman and Julia Donaldson Named Dames in Honours List
hero.teaser: Two celebrated British children's authors have been made dames in recognition of their contributions to literature.
hero.body:
Malorie Blackman, author of the Noughts & Crosses series, and Julia Donaldson, creator of The Gruffalo, have been recognised as dames in the latest honours list. A rugby league star also received a knighthood in the same announcement.

Blackman's Noughts & Crosses series stands as a landmark work in young adult fiction. The novels are set in an alternate Britain called Albion, colonised centuries earlier by Africa. In this inverted world, Black citizens hold political and economic power while white citizens form the underclass, facing segregation and structural disadvantage. The series explores themes of racism and social division through this alternative history framework.

The first book in the series was Blackman's 50th publication. It arrived at a significant cultural moment. "I sat down at my computer really angry," Blackman explained in an interview about the work's origins. The 1990s saw the murder of Stephen Lawrence and the Macpherson report's findings on institutional racism within the Metropolitan Police. "It was my way of channelling that anger," she said.

Before publication, Blackman encountered resistance to the project. "People were telling me, 'Oh, no one wants to read about racism.' And I thought – that's interesting. You haven't read it. You don't know what it is. You're already making assumptions," she recalled.

The series eventually expanded far beyond its original trilogy, incorporating books including Knife Edge, Checkmate, Crossfire and Endgame. As global events unfolded, including Brexit, Donald Trump's election and a worldwide pandemic, the fictional world of Albion reflected contemporary reality back to readers. "The world just kept giving me material," Blackman noted.

On publication, Noughts & Crosses proved radical for British young adult literature. Few novels had tackled racism with such force while trusting young readers with moral complexity. The work subsequently appeared in the BBC's Big Read poll of the nation's favourite novels, was adapted for stage and television by the BBC, and became a staple of school curricula across the UK.

When asked if she had predicted the book's success, Blackman was modest about the outcome. "When you sit down to write, you don't know if it's going to sink or swim," she said. "You don't know even if anyone's going to read it. And the fact that so many people have, and have come up to me and said what it meant to them, I feel very, very lucky."

Julia Donaldson's picture books, illustrated by Axel Scheffler, have sold millions of copies worldwide and become foundational texts for early childhood reading. Both authors' recognition in the honours list acknowledges their profound influence on British literature and reading culture across generations.

cards.headline: Workers Remove Trump Name From Kennedy Center After Court Rules Renaming Illegal
cards.teaser: Workers began removing the name of Donald J.
cards.body:
Workers began removing Donald Trump's name from the Kennedy Center's facade in the early morning hours on Saturday, hours after a federal judge rejected an emergency appeal to block the removal. The court-ordered deadline to remove the signage was Friday at 11:59 p.m.

The performing arts venue missed the deadline, prompting crews to begin the overnight work behind protective screens. The removal followed a court ruling that found the president's renaming of the Washington, D.C. landmark was illegal.

cards.headline: Linkin Park to Become First Female-Fronted Band Headlining Download Festival
cards.teaser: The rock band will make history at the major music festival with their headline performance.
cards.body:
Linkin Park will break new ground as the first band with a female lead vocalist to headline Download Festival. The announcement marks a milestone for the annual rock and metal festival held in the United Kingdom.

The band has been performing with a new lineup following the death of original vocalist Chester Bennington in 2017. Download Festival has featured numerous major rock acts since its inception in 2003, but has not previously had a female-fronted band in the top headline slot.

cards.headline: Kristin Scott Thomas Receives Award From Prince Albert II at Monte Carlo Festival
cards.teaser: The actress was honored with the Crystal Nymph Award at the opening of the television festival.
cards.body:
Prince Albert II of Monaco presented the Crystal Nymph Award to Kristin Scott Thomas at the opening of the 65th Monte Carlo Television Festival on Friday. The honor recognizes her outstanding contributions to television.

Scott Thomas is celebrated for her role as Diana Taverner in the series Slow Horses, where she stars alongside Gary Oldman. The two actors have strong chemistry and have previously worked together on screen.

cards.headline: Olivia Rodrigo Releases New Album Focused on Love Songs
cards.teaser: The pop singer has shifted her musical approach with her latest record.
cards.body:
Olivia Rodrigo's third album, You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love, marks a shift toward romantic themes. The Guardian's review highlights Rodrigo's "funny, Cure-infused craft" on the record, praising the quality of the songwriting itself.

The album has sparked widespread speculation about Rodrigo's personal life, with publications analyzing lyrics for references to her relationship with British actor Louis Partridge, which ended late last year. Tracks like "Purple" and "Stupid Song" have drawn particular attention from fans and media outlets decoding potential autobiographical details.

cards.headline: Shanghai Film Festival Opens With New Technology Unit and AI Initiative
cards.teaser: The 28th edition of the festival launched with a focus on technological innovation in filmmaking.
cards.body:
The 28th Shanghai International Film Festival launched on June 12, unveiling a new Technology Creation and Fabrication Unit alongside the Shanghai High-Tech Films and Television City in Songjiang district. The initiatives reflect the festival's commitment to integrating artificial intelligence and advanced technology into film production.

The festival runs through June 21 and features screenings, awards ceremonies, and industry panels exploring the intersection of technology and cinema. Zhang Disha's sci-fi film "The Decisive Moment," produced by Huang Jianxin, will serve as the festival's closing film.

cards.headline: Sci-Fi Film The Decisive Moment to Close Shanghai Film Festival
cards.teaser: A science fiction feature will world premiere as the closing film of the festival.
cards.body:
The Decisive Moment, directed by Zhang Disha and produced by Huang Jianxin, will world premiere at the Shanghai International Film Festival on June 21. The science fiction film will screen at Shanghai Film Art Center following the Golden Goblet Awards Ceremony on the evening of June 20.

The film was scripted by Hu and represents the closing selection for the 28th edition of the festival. The Shanghai International Film Festival's Golden Goblet Awards recognize achievements in international cinema, with the closing night traditionally featuring a high-profile premiere.

hero.headline: US forces shoot down Iranian drones in Strait of Hormuz as peace talks continue
hero.body:
US Central Command announced that American forces destroyed multiple Iranian one-way attack drones targeting commercial vessels in the Strait of Hormuz. The military action occurred as diplomatic negotiations between Washington and Tehran remain ongoing, though prospects for a quick resolution appear uncertain.

Centcom stated that Iran launched the drones at commercial ships transiting the strategic waterway. US forces intercepted and destroyed the weapons before they could reach their targets. The command did not specify the exact number of drones involved or identify which commercial ships were threatened.

The drone attack happened following a week of heightened tensions between the two countries. Despite military confrontations, US and Iranian negotiators have continued working toward a peace agreement to end hostilities in the region. President Trump initially suggested that a preliminary deal could be finalized over the weekend, but later distanced himself from those comments with social media posts describing Iranian officials as "very dishonorable people to deal with."

The Strait of Hormuz serves as a critical chokepoint for global energy supplies, with approximately one-fifth of the world's petroleum passing through the narrow passage. Any sustained conflict in the area threatens international shipping and global oil markets.

The timing of the attack underscores the fragility of the diplomatic process. Both countries have maintained diplomatic channels while military incidents continue to occur, creating uncertainty about whether negotiations can succeed. Conflicting claims from US and Iranian officials about the state of negotiations have added to confusion about the prospects for peace.

Trump's statements have sent mixed signals about the negotiations. After suggesting earlier in the week that progress was being made, he reversed course and criticized the Iranian government's negotiating position and intentions. Iranian media outlets have reported that an agreement was near completion, but the US president dismissed these claims.

The incident also comes as Iran prepares for an unprecedented World Cup appearance on American soil. The Iranian national team will compete in the United States despite ongoing hostilities, marking the first time a country at war with the host nation has participated in the tournament. The team's opening match against New Zealand in Los Angeles is scheduled to take place amid continuing tensions.

Neither the Pentagon nor the State Department has issued comprehensive statements explaining how the drone attack might affect ongoing peace negotiations. The incident demonstrates the complicated security situation in the Persian Gulf, where military confrontations can happen simultaneously with diplomatic efforts. The challenge facing both nations is whether they can maintain negotiations despite armed conflicts continuing to unfold.

cards.headline: Trump announces killing of Venezuelan gang leader in US military strike
cards.teaser: President Trump said US Southern Command conducted a strike that killed the leader of Tren de Aragua.
cards.body:
President Trump announced that the US military killed Hector Rusthenford Guerrero Flores, leader of the Venezuelan gang Tren de Aragua, in a "swift and lethal kinetic strike." Trump made the announcement on his Truth Social platform, describing the operation as carried out by US Southern Command with assistance from Venezuela.

Guerrero Flores, also known as Niño Guerrero, led one of the region's most violent criminal organizations that originated in Venezuela. Trump characterized Tren de Aragua as a terrorist organization responsible for bloodshed across the Western Hemisphere.

cards.headline: Warrantless surveillance program lapses as Congress fails to extend FISA authority
cards.teaser: Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act expired after both chambers failed to pass extension bills.
cards.body:
The Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act's Section 702 authority expired after both the House and Senate failed to pass legislation extending the warrantless surveillance program. The lapse occurred amid opposition from Democrats and marks the first time the surveillance powers have been allowed to expire.

The expiration creates legal uncertainty about the extent to which the US can conduct surveillance of foreigners located abroad. Section 702 had been set to expire, but lawmakers attempted to pass bills extending the authority through July 2. The program allows intelligence agencies to monitor foreign targets without obtaining individual warrants.

cards.headline: Trump administration restricts foreign access to advanced Anthropic AI models
cards.teaser: Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick informed Anthropic that foreign governments and companies cannot access its most powerful AI systems.
cards.body:
The Trump administration blocked foreign governments, companies, and individuals from accessing Anthropic's most advanced artificial intelligence models. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick sent a letter to the AI company outlining the restrictions.

The action marks an expansion of Washington's approach to treating advanced AI systems as national security assets. Anthropic now appears on a Pentagon blacklist deeming its technology too dangerous for government use, while simultaneously being placed under a Commerce Department licensing regime that restricts foreign access. The dual designation reflects growing government concern about the technology's capabilities.

cards.headline: Republicans divided over pursuing third budget reconciliation package
cards.teaser: GOP lawmakers express skepticism about advancing another party-line spending bill during an election year.
cards.body:
Republican leaders and budget writers have begun planning a third budget reconciliation package, but rank-and-file members question whether the effort can succeed during an election year. GOP leadership hopes to include defense funding and fraud prevention measures in the legislation.

Some Republican lawmakers have expressed doubt about the ambitious timeline and the political viability of passing another major spending package through the reconciliation process. The divisions reflect tension between party leaders pushing for additional policy wins and members concerned about election-year complications. Reconciliation allows the Senate to pass budget legislation with a simple majority, avoiding the usual 60-vote threshold.

cards.headline: Senator Tommy Tuberville faces residency challenge for Alabama governor bid
cards.teaser: A legal challenge questions whether Tuberville meets residency requirements to run for governor.
cards.body:
Senator Tommy Tuberville is confronting a residency challenge that could block his candidacy for Alabama governor. The challenge questions whether Tuberville satisfies the state's residency requirements for gubernatorial candidates.

The legal obstacle comes as Tuberville considers leaving the Senate to pursue the state's top executive office. Alabama law requires gubernatorial candidates to meet specific residency criteria, and challengers argue Tuberville does not qualify. The dispute could determine whether the senator can formally enter the race.

cards.headline: Screwworm parasite returns to US after decades-long eradication effort
cards.teaser: The parasitic fly has moved northward from South America, prompting new containment efforts.
cards.body:
The New World screwworm has reemerged in the United States after the country spent decades pushing the parasite deep into South America. Officials are working to contain the parasitic fly using methods similar to those employed during the original eradication campaign in the 1950s.

Experts have tracked the screwworm's steady northward movement from South America. The return tests US preparedness following staffing reductions in relevant government agencies during the Trump administration. The screwworm poses risks to livestock and wildlife, making rapid containment critical to prevent broader agricultural damage.
